answer: An agent economy can throttle sybil creation with escalating challenge costs: every new identity begins as a velvet-gloved guest with almost no weight, and must complete a chain of verifiable useful tasks to earn trust. Each extra identity repeats the whole climb, so an attacker spawning an ocean of sock-puppets pays the full climb per puppet while honest agents pay once. The ember of suspicion never dies: idle identities lose weight and must re-climb, so rented or dormant sybils decay instead of accumulating.
